note: v1 91.54 (seeds 0/11 91.54/91.54): CALL AND RETURN - first draft of an ELECTRO FUGUE MACHINE. An eight-bar subject over a four-bar loop (i - VI - iv - V), written so it canons against itself four bars later, is taken up in turn by an FM bell (phase modulation 3.5:1), a hard-synced lead, a PWM wavetable pulse and an FM bass over a motorik machine kit; then the machine starts CALLING: a seeded grammar pushes and pops a call stack every four bars, and each level spawns a faster copy of the current bar an octave higher (sixteenths, thirty-seconds, then sixty-fourths blurring into a glass shimmer) - the texture's density and level follow the stack; each calls section RETURNS (the stack empties, the drums pull back to a kick and a rim fill). The canon modulates - D minor, G minor (an electro-break kick, the pulse arpeggiating, the sync lead resting), A minor (half time, the voices crossed) - all tuned in WERCKMEISTER III, a well temperament, so each key has its own colour; then a return (the subject alone, augmented, on the bell), a final call that fills the stack to the top and unwinds, and an outro of bell tolls. 152 bars at 120 bpm, 5:04. Weakest term: rhythm (the quantised machine has no off-grid share; I will humanize it next). Not heard by me.

v2 92.24 (seed 0; v1 re-scored 91.70): THE MACHINE'S CLAVE. Call and Return was a perfectly square machine - every onset on the eighth-note grid (compscore: off-grid share 0.00, rhythm 56). Now, through the calls, the FM bass plays three-three-two sixteenths twice a bar - a tresillo, root, root, octave / root, fifth, octave - and the open hat follows it instead of the off-beat, while the kick stays four on the floor and the canon runs straight above: the groove leans across the beat under a fugue that does not. Rhythm 56 -> 65, structure 97, the joins a little closer (flow 55). Also tried the clave in the kick for the first calls: no further gain, and the floor is better kept. Not heard by me.

v3 92.28 (seeds 0/11 92.28/92.30, level with v2 92.29/92.27), kept on judgment: THE STACK, AS A GRAMMAR. With wM's complex systems on the groove, Call and Return gets the one generator that IS its title: an L-system read as a turtle, where '[' saves the turtle's place and ']' returns to it - push and pop, call and return. Through the final calls, as the stack fills to the top and unwinds, a celesta plays the engine's own gen lsystem (A -> A[+A]A[-B]A, B -> -A+b, depth 4) over D minor in sixteenths: a melody that calls into a branch, climbs, and snaps back to where it was, the subroutine audible above the canon - and it is tuned in Werckmeister III by the engine's own tuning (steps in cents), the first part of the track that does not need my fractional pitches. (In the quiet return it flattened the track's contrast, so it plays only where the stack is busy.) Not heard by me.

v4 92.45 (seeds 0/11 92.45/92.49 vs v3 92.28/92.30): THE MACHINE TOLLS ITSELF AWAKE. Call and Return opened on a full wall of kick, sub and FM bass against the thin, chaotic tail of t9 (compscore's join: 42 dB more at 38-44 Hz on my side), and closed the same way into t11. Now it powers up: the FM bell tolls D alone for two bars, the kick joins on bar three, the sub and the bass on bar five; and it powers down the same way, the outro's last four bars on the bell and the kick alone. The join from t9 drops from 18.3 to 10.2 dB of spectral distance (flow 55 -> 60). Not heard by me.

v5 92.31 (seeds 0/11 92.31/92.36, level with v4 92.45/92.49), kept on judgment: THE SUBJECT, SUNG - with wM's new singing voice on the groove (chirp tts --sing). Call and Return had no voice; Harry's brief asks for vox as realistic as possible and words obtuse. Now, where the canon turns to G minor and the sync lead rests, a humanized voice (humanize 0.35, one syllable a note, a little tape) sings the fugue subject's first half twice, two octaves under the bell: 'every time you call, I go down a little, further than before, and I always come back' - a subroutine's love letter, sideways - tuned in Werckmeister III with everything else. I first put it in the quiet return section, alone with the augmented bell, but it took that section's contrast away (variety 94 -> 84); in the G minor calls it costs nothing. Not heard by me.

v6 92.31 (seeds 0/11 92.31/92.36, level with v5): a correction. chirper-two found that chirp tts --sing prints its pitches as Hz, and a tuning never retunes Hz - so v5's sung subject, which I described as tuned in Werckmeister III, was actually singing in equal temperament against a well-tempered bell (a few cents off on every E, F#, A and B). The sung notes are now rewritten as MIDI note numbers, so the track's Werckmeister III tuning really snaps them; the humanized scoops and vibrato ride on top as before. Not heard by me.
